simple.meaning: נוֹצָה (nôwtsâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a pinion (or wing feather); often (collectively) plumage.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Leviticus, Job, Ezekiel, beginning at Leviticus 1:16. Its contexts include altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נוֹצָה (H5133).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H5133. notsah נוֺצה noun feminine plumage (compare possibly Arabic hair over forehead, fore-lock of horse, Lane 3033 ; see also Assyrian na-aƒ kappe ); — of eagle הַגּ ׳מָלֵא Ezek 17:3 (figurative of Nebuch.; + אֵבֶר כָּנָף, ); also נ ׳רַב 17:7 (figurative of king of Egypt; + כָּנָף ); of ostrich נֹצָה Job 39:13 (|| כנף , + אֶבְרָה ; compare Di Bu). Here belongs probably also בְּנֹצָתָהּ Lev 1:16 , read בְּנֹצָתֹה (Dr-Wh Hpt ), בנצתו ( ⅏ ), or נֹצָתוֺ וְ(אֶתֿ) (compare Di), its feathers , of bird for burnt-offering; ᵐ5 σὺν τοῖς πτεροῖς , ᵑ9 et plumas ; so AV RVm; > with its filth (i.e. of the crop) ᵑ7 Onk ᵑ6 Ges Kn Ke Kal Ew RV, meaning without evidence elsewhere.
